raw_response:
I’m still doing wheat-maize on all 9.5 mu. That’s what I know best, and with a small place like mine I can’t take big risks. Last year the wheat and maize were both acceptable, not great but steady, and around here everybody still relies on this rotation. I’ve farmed 30 years, so I mostly go by what I’ve seen on my own land and what the other farmers nearby are doing. The extension people talk about careful rates, but in real life I look at the crop stand, leaf color, rain, and whether I have enough cash in hand. Since some people in my family work off-farm, labor at home is not always enough, so I keep the management practical and timed to the usual season. I have well water, so for wheat I will not save too much on irrigation, because if wheat misses water at the key stage, the yield loss is hard to recover. For fertilizer, I will use a bit more on wheat than maize, because wheat responds clearly on my fields. Maize goes in right after wheat harvest, so I need a simple turnaround, fast tillage, and quick sowing. I won’t do anything fancy this year, just the usual way that is reliable and fits my money and labor.
